prompt: The Biden presidency, United States 2021 to 2025
title: The Biden presidency
description: You won the White House, but the Senate is split evenly and only your Vice President's vote breaks a tie. Hospitals are still full and prices are starting to climb. Within a year, Russia will invade Ukraine. And one senator from West Virginia can sink any bill you send.

face.name: Bernie Sanders
face.role: Senator for Vermont, chair of the Budget Committee

blocs.name: Dockworkers
blocs.description: Load and unload the harbor's ships, organized under the Keelwright Guild.

blocs.name: Merchants
blocs.description: Own the trading houses and warehouses along Northpier.

blocs.name: Fisherfolk
blocs.description: Work the fishing fleets out of Saltmarsh and Isle Row.

blocs.name: Clergy
blocs.description: Keep the tide calendar and run the Uplands temples.

blocs.name: Students
blocs.description: Apprentices and scholars at the Ferry Quarter academies.

starts.premise: You are Joe Biden, the 46th President of the United States.
You are Joe Biden, the 46th President of the United States.
You are Joe Biden, the 46th President of the United States.

problems: Prices are rising faster than wages
The rescue bill needs a vote by turn 3
The Senate is split 50 to 50, so one senator can sink any bill
Every bill goes through the Senate: 100 seats, 50 that vote with you and 50 against, and your Vice President breaks a tie.
Your cabinet picks need the Senate too, because it confirms every post.
The Supreme Court has no vote on you, but it can strike down your executive orders. Orders that go around Congress cost you its support.
The midterms come at turn 10. At turn 20 five groups hold the final vote on you.
The east mole needs repair before the autumn gales.

escalations.name: The Herald Turns
escalations.headline: The harbor's broadsheet runs a season of hostile notices against the council.

escalations.name: The Grand Consensus
escalations.headline: Every decree now needs the grand consensus to pass.

escalations.name: The Lean Tide
escalations.headline: Trade falls and two guild patrons pull their support.

escalations.name: The Whisper Season
escalations.headline: Four councilors face whispered investigations.

escalations.name: The Short Reckoning
escalations.headline: The reckoning's thresholds tighten to twenty and sixty.

escalations.name: The Broken Bench
escalations.headline: The midterm draw flips eight seats against the sitting consul.

escalations.name: The Steep Toll
escalations.headline: Petitions to patrons now cost half again as much.

escalations.name: The Restless Quarter
escalations.headline: Pledges must be kept by the eighth and sixteenth tide.

escalations.name: The Bare Treasury
escalations.headline: Patron contributions are cut in half.

escalations.name: The Sharp Bench
escalations.headline: The temple court strikes decrees at a lower bar.

escalations.name: The Rival's Purse
escalations.headline: Rival factions double their canvass spending.

escalations.name: The Quiet Quarter
escalations.headline: Turnout among the council's own blocs drops sharply.

escalations.name: The Loose Bench
escalations.headline: Co-faction loyalty erodes on every vote.

escalations.name: The Jeering Gallery
escalations.headline: Boos in the gallery count for more against every decree.

escalations.name: The Tired Harbor
escalations.headline: No relief cards are drawn for the rest of the term.

escalations.name: The Leaky Hull
escalations.headline: Petitions risk becoming headlines a third of the time.

escalations.name: The War Tide
escalations.headline: Naval matters always face the grand consensus, and the treasury bleeds each tide.

escalations.name: The Lean Harvest
escalations.headline: Standing falls hard in ten seeded wards, some more than others.

escalations.name: The Contested Line
escalations.headline: Party mood opens the term already low.

escalations.name: The Foreign Hand
escalations.headline: Two wards lose faith in the reckoning before it is cast.

test.name: the final vote
test.win: The council keeps its mandate for another term.

pork.label: Promise a project
pork.text: The Consul promises a new warehouse for the district.

favor.label: Trade a favor
favor.text: The Consul offers to back the councilor's own petition next tide.

threat.label: Threaten a challenger
threat.text: The Consul threatens to back a rival in the next canvass.

ruler.removedBy: Democratic Party can call the final vote early if its support falls below its line.

holders.name: Congress

persona.name: Chuck Schumer
persona.bio: 100 senators, two from each state: 48 Democrats, 2 independents who vote with them, 50 Republicans. Budget bills pass with 50 and your Vice President's vote.
persona.tell: Send us the bill. We decide what it costs.

wants: Congress wants its say on every dollar you spend.
redLines: Ending the filibuster by a party-line rules change

holders.name: Supreme Court

persona.name: John Roberts
persona.role: Chief Justice of the United States
persona.bio: Nine justices appointed for life: six named by Republican presidents, three by Democrats. Chief Justice John Roberts.
persona.tell: The Court reads the order against the statute, not the headlines.

wants: The Court wants orders that stay inside the law.
redLines: Defying a ruling of the Court

face.name: John Roberts
face.role: Chief Justice of the United States

holders.name: Federal Reserve

persona.name: Jerome Powell
persona.bio: The central bank: a Board of Governors in Washington and 12 regional banks. Chair Jerome Powell's term ends in February 2022.
persona.tell: We will keep at it until prices come down.

wants: The Fed wants room to fight rising prices.
redLines: Ordering the Fed to hold rates down

holders.name: NATO allies

persona.name: Jens Stoltenberg
persona.bio: The 29 other members of the alliance. Germany, France, Britain and Poland set the tone in Brussels under Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg.
persona.tell: The alliance needs Washington at the front of it.

wants: The allies want a firm line on Russia.
redLines: Doubting the Article 5 promise in public

holders.name: The American public

persona.name: Deb Kowalski
persona.bio: About 258 million adults. In November 2020, 81 million voted for you and 74 million for Donald Trump.
persona.tell: Groceries cost more every week. Fix that first.

wants: The American public wants prices down and jobs back.
redLines: Sending troops against protesters in US cities

holders.name: China

persona.name: Wang Yi
persona.bio: The People's Republic under Xi Jinping and the Communist Party. About $370 billion a year of its goods face US tariffs set in 2018 and 2019.
persona.tell: Lift the tariffs, and we can talk about the rest.

wants: Beijing wants tariffs lifted and no new chip bans.
responses: Cuts off chips and rare earths

glance.strike: Cuts off chips and rare earths

holders.name: Democratic Party

persona.name: Nancy Pelosi
persona.role: Speaker of the House, San Francisco
persona.bio: The party that nominated you: about 48 million registered Democrats, the Senate caucus, and a House majority of 222 to 213 under Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
persona.tell: We ran on this agenda. Now deliver it.

wants: Your party wants the agenda you ran on.

face.name: Nancy Pelosi
face.role: Speaker of the House, San Francisco

holders.name: Republican Party

persona.name: Mitch McConnell
persona.bio: The other party: 50 senators under Mitch McConnell, 213 House members, about 36 million registered Republicans. Donald Trump is still its loudest voice.
persona.tell: Not one more dollar without cuts.

wants: The Republicans want less spending and a tighter border.
redLines: A federal law over how states run elections

holders.name: The bond markets

persona.name: Ruth Adler
persona.role: Head of rates, a London bank
persona.bio: The holders of about $22 trillion of Treasury debt: pension funds, banks, and central banks from Tokyo to Beijing.
persona.tell: Show us a budget that adds up.

wants: The bond markets want a budget that adds up.
redLines: Missing a payment on Treasury debt

face.name: Ruth Adler
face.role: Head of rates, a London bank

treasury.name: Federal funds
treasury.for: Pays for programs, relief and deals.
treasury.fails: you cannot spend until a revenue law passes.

authority.name: Authority
authority.for: The price of acting at all. Every act costs some.
authority.fails: you can only speak and spend.

chest.name: Campaign cash
chest.for: Buys reach for your addresses and votes on the floor.
chest.fails: your voice stops carrying and rivals outspend you.

briefing.situation: You won the White House, but the Senate is split evenly and only your Vice President's vote breaks a tie. Hospitals are still full and prices are starting to climb. Within a year, Russia will invade Ukraine. And one senator from West Virginia can sink any bill you send.
briefing.room: Every act wins some groups and costs you others. This is who they are, what they can do to you, and how much each one counts at the end.
briefing.you: Each act costs one ledger and can pay another. The red tick on each bar is where it fails.
